description: ADR-028 D1 (#924 / #1002 / #1234 / #1235) federation revocation reconciler — the operational field view for the un-revoke tamper-evidence control. Source metrics are emitted by the federation-reconciler Deployment's /metrics (job=federation-reconciler, port 9099; helm/federation-reconciler runs _federation_revocation_reconciler.py). All eleven metrics are platform-global with ZERO labels, so there is no per-tenant template variable. Panel thresholds are aligned 1:1 to the seven platform alerts (FederationRevocationTamperSuspected > 0, FederationRevocationReconcileStale time()-ts > 1800s, FederationRevocationEvidenceChannelDown channel_up == 0, FederationGatewayRevocationLoadFailure > 0, FederationRevocationLiveSetRejected > 0, FederationGatewayRevokedSetReloadRejected > 0, FederationGatewayRevokedSetMissing > 0 — the only one of the gateway trio where the enforcement plane is EMPTY rather than frozen, #1236) so the dashboard and the pager agree on what is bad. Rows map to the runbook's five chaos-validation scenarios: fail-closed / liveness, schema-drift, fail-open (拍頻), the tamper headline, and the evidence-channel canary; the enforcement-plane staleness pair (#1235) is a second summary row with no chaos scenario of its own yet. Behavioural contract: tests/dx/test_federation_revocation_dashboard.py.

panels.title: Tamper status
panels.description: HEADLINE SECURITY SIGNAL (ADR-028 D1). Suspected un-revokes: token_ids the off-store revocation log says are revoked and NOT yet expired, but ABSENT from the live revoked set. 0 = clean; >0 = a write-capable actor may have dropped a revocation while carrying the legitimate SA identity (which the #926 identity audit cannot see). Threshold aligned to the FederationRevocationTamperSuspected alert (>0, for 5m, critical). a11y (ADR-012 / WCAG 1.4.1): state is symbol + text, never colour alone. ✓ Clean is a live all-clear ONLY when Reconciler freshness is green — a fail-closed / stale pass does NOT refresh this gauge (it holds its last value), so read the two panels together.

panels.title: Reconciler freshness
panels.description: Seconds since the last SUCCESSFUL reconcile (time() - last_reconcile_timestamp). A fail-closed pass (VictoriaLogs query or revoked.txt read failed) deliberately does NOT refresh the timestamp, so staleness surfaces here rather than as a false all-clear. <1800 = fresh; >=1800 = the un-revoke detection is BLIND. Threshold aligned to the FederationRevocationReconcileStale alert (time()-ts > 1800s = 30m, for 10m, critical). NOTE: on a fresh deploy the timestamp is 0, so this reads a very large delta (stale-by-default) until the first successful pass. a11y: symbol + text.

panels.title: Evidence channel
panels.description: Is the un-revoke detection actually RECEIVING evidence? (ADR-028 D1 / #1234) tenant-api emits a content-free heartbeat canary every 5m down the SAME Vector transform and sink path as real revocation events; this reads 1 when the reconciler saw it in its 30m window. 1 = the channel is live and a clean Tamper status means something. 0 = the evidence path (tenant-api log -> Vector origin_split -> federation_evidence -> VictoriaLogs) is SEVERED, so the reconciler is reporting all-clear over an EMPTY feed — Tamper status can never leave ✓ Clean and Reconciler freshness stays green. Without this panel an empty channel is indistinguishable from 'no revocations happened'. Threshold aligned to the FederationRevocationEvidenceChannelDown alert (== 0, for 15m, critical). NOTE: this reads 0 on a fresh deploy until the first successful reconcile pass (the alert's 15m window is the grace period), and a VictoriaLogs outage does NOT drive it to 0 — the reconciler holds the previous value and surfaces that as staleness instead. a11y: symbol + text.

panels.title: Gateway fail-open
panels.description: Gateway revoked-set read failures in the recent (~10m) window. The federation-gateway fails OPEN by design when it cannot read revoked.txt — revoked tokens ARE accepted until their TTL (<=4h). 0 = OK; >0 = the ADR-028 named Risk Acceptance is active and revoked tokens are being honoured. Threshold aligned to the FederationGatewayRevocationLoadFailure alert (>0, for 2m, warning). The fail-closed hardening is tracked in #996. a11y: symbol + text.

panels.title: Coverage integrity
panels.description: Event-filtered log rows that carried the federation_token_revoked marker but FAILED to parse last pass — a tenant-api event-schema drift signal that silently narrows reconciliation coverage. 0 = intact; >0 = coverage is eroded (a fully-drifted feed would otherwise reconcile to a clean, healthy zero while a real un-revoke went unseen — ADR-028 D3 honest boundary). No dedicated alert yet (defer-with-trigger per ADR-028), so this panel is the primary signal. a11y: symbol + text.

panels.title: Revoked-set contract — file
panels.description: ENFORCEMENT-PLANE STALENESS, cause side (ADR-028 D1 / #1235). Lines in the mounted revoked.txt that violate the token-id line contract, as THIS reconciler reads the file. The gateway applies the same contract and discards the WHOLE reload on a violation, keeping the set it had already loaded — so >0 means the enforcement plane is frozen on a pre-violation revoked set: every revocation issued since that line appeared is NOT in force, and a gateway worker whose FIRST load hit it has no previous set and is enforcing nothing. ⛔ This is NOT 'Gateway fail-open': there the list is unreadable and revoked tokens ARE being let through; here the list is readable and is being refused. ⛔ Tamper status will NOT show this — it compares the audit log against the FILE, which does contain the newer revocations. Threshold aligned to the FederationRevocationLiveSetRejected alert (>0, for 10m, critical). a11y (ADR-012 / WCAG 1.4.1): state is symbol + text, never colour alone.

panels.title: Revoked-set reload — gateway
panels.description: ENFORCEMENT-PLANE STALENESS, the gateway's own account (ADR-028 D1 / #1235). Reload-refusal warnings read back off the gateway's own log stream in the recent (~10m) window — what the ENFORCEMENT plane says it did, not this process's second reading of the file. Deliberately NOT redundant with the panel to its left: the two ends read different kubelet projections of the same ConfigMap at different moments, so the file can read clean here while the gateway is still refusing; conversely this one stays silent for any cause that never produced the warning. Either can be non-zero alone — read them together. ⛔ COLD START: check the gateway pods' start times against the first of these warnings; a pod whose FIRST load hit the violation has no previous set and is enforcing NOTHING, which is the fail-open posture rather than the frozen one. Threshold aligned to the FederationGatewayRevokedSetReloadRejected alert (>0, for 10m, critical). a11y: symbol + text.

panels.title: Revoked-set — MISSING
panels.description: THE ENFORCEMENT PLANE HAS NO LIST AT ALL (ADR-028 §fail-open / #1236). Warnings, in the recent (~10m) window, where the gateway reported its revoked-set file is ABSENT. ⛔ Read this differently from the two panels to its left: those mean the gateway is FROZEN on a set it already had — stale, but still rejecting. This one means it holds NOTHING, so every revoked token is being honoured until its TTL (≤4h). It is the ADR-028 §相鄰破口 attack shape (delete / unmount the projected key) and equally what a namespace misconfiguration looks like (#1313) — a ConfigMap is namespace-scoped, so the volume only resolves one in the gateway's OWN namespace. Until #1236 this state produced no signal at all: the Lua's missing branch returns normally from inside its pcall, so neither other warning fired. Threshold aligned to the FederationGatewayRevokedSetMissing alert (>0, for 5m, critical). a11y: symbol + text.

panels.title: Reconciler staleness (fail-closed / liveness)
panels.description: CHAOS SCENARIO: fail-closed. Seconds since last successful reconcile over time; the 1800s line is the FederationRevocationReconcileStale threshold. Healthy: time()-ts oscillates near 0 (sawtooth on the reconcile interval, 300s). Bad: climbs past 1800 and keeps rising = VictoriaLogs / revoked.txt read is failing and the pass no longer refreshes the timestamp (fail-closed, never a false all-clear). To validate: pause the VictoriaLogs Service and watch this cross 1800.

panels.title: Reconcile error rate (fail-closed)
panels.description: CHAOS SCENARIO: fail-closed (companion). rate(federation_revocation_reconcile_errors_total[5m]) — the fail-closed marker. Each failed pass (query / read / reconcile error) bumps this monotonic counter and leaves last_reconcile_ts frozen. Healthy: flat 0. Bad: sustained positive rate AND the staleness panel to the left climbs together = the reconciler is fail-closed and going stale, not silently clearing.

panels.title: Events checked
panels.description: federation_revocation_events_checked — the number of still-comfortably-live revocation events reconciled in the last pass (the working set the tamper check ran over). Context, not an alarm: a sudden drop toward 0 while traffic is expected can hint the query window is returning nothing (read with the staleness and coverage panels).

panels.title: Events dropped (schema-drift)
panels.description: CHAOS SCENARIO: schema-drift. federation_revocation_events_dropped over time — rows that carried the federation_token_revoked marker but could not be parsed (missing field / bad timestamp) = tenant-api event-schema drift. Healthy: flat 0. Bad: any sustained >0 means reconciliation coverage is silently eroding. To validate: inject a federation_token_revoked event missing a required field and watch this rise (visible, not silent).

panels.title: Coverage erosion ratio (schema-drift)
panels.description: CHAOS SCENARIO: schema-drift (proportional view). dropped / (checked + dropped) — the fraction of the event feed the reconciler could NOT parse. clamp_min(...,1) guards the denominator so an idle feed (checked=0, dropped=0) reads 0, NOT 0/0=NaN. 0 = fully covered; approaching 1 = the feed has almost entirely drifted (near-total blindness while the tamper gauge would still read a deceptively healthy 0). unit = percentunit.

panels.title: Gateway revoked-set read failures (fail-open / 拍頻)
panels.description: CHAOS SCENARIO: fail-open + 拍頻 (beat-frequency). federation_gateway_revocation_load_errors over the recent window; the >0 line is the FederationGatewayRevocationLoadFailure threshold (for 2m, warning). Healthy: flat 0. Bad: >0 = the gateway is failing OPEN and revoked tokens are honoured until TTL. 拍頻 WATCH: the reconcile interval (300s) beats against the Prometheus scrape interval; oscillation of this gauge right at the for:2m boundary can flap the alert. If you see it toggling in and out of firing near 2m, tune the for: window or the reconcile interval (runbook chaos step 4).

panels.title: Suspected un-revokes (tamper headline)
panels.description: HEADLINE. federation_revocation_tamper_suspected over time; the >0 line is the FederationRevocationTamperSuspected threshold. >0 sustained for 5m = critical: a revoked-but-live token is absent from the live set (ADR-028 un-revoke). Any sustained excursion above 0 is a security event — query VictoriaLogs for event:"federation_token_revoked" for the opaque token_id(s), resolve the tenant from the store at IR time (D3), diff against the live store, and if malicious restore the revocation from git. ✓ Clean is a live all-clear ONLY when Reconciler freshness is green — a fail-closed / stale pass does NOT refresh this gauge (it holds its last value), so read the two panels together.

panels.title: Heartbeat canary — 30m window liveness
panels.description: CHAOS SCENARIO: evidence-channel severance (ADR-028 D1 / #1234). federation_revocation_channel_up (0/1) plotted with federation_revocation_heartbeats_seen (canary rows in the 30m window). Healthy: channel_up flat at 1 and heartbeats_seen steady around 5-6 (tenant-api emits every 5m into a 30m window — that margin is why one lost log line cannot page). Bad: heartbeats_seen decays toward 0 and channel_up drops to 0 = the tenant-api -> Vector -> VictoriaLogs evidence path is severed and the un-revoke control is reporting all-clear over an empty feed. Read heartbeats_seen FIRST: a partial decay (6 -> 2) is the early warning that channel_up has not yet crossed, and a sudden cliff to 0 points at a producer-side event-name rename or a Vector selector change rather than a slow leak. To validate: scale tenant-api to 0 (or set evidenceChannel.events to a name it does not emit) and watch heartbeats_seen fall to 0, then channel_up to 0, then FederationRevocationEvidenceChannelDown fire after for:15m.
